Hi, welcome to our presentation of DeepLane, a new corpus for Dremantech level and on the sentence level. My name is Ligina Stodden and I will guide you through the first part of the presentation. Let's first define text simplification. Text simplification is a process of a adapting a text to improve the text comprehension of it for a specific target group, as people receiving problems on non-native speakers. To train a text identification model, we require parallel pairs of text, for example, of documents sentences. And the example here, you can see a parallel aligned sentence pair of a complex German sentence and it's through the translation into plain language. To simplify the sentence, different techniques are possible as you can see in the example, such as lexical substitution, clostulation, clostalition reordering or insertion of ports. We now propose our new corporality plane. Because in the recent years there were some problems with existing corporal. So for example, this corporate year are too small to train a decent vacation model on. models which are proposed in recent years are all automatically aligned, which means they can be our error prone in their alignments. Therefore, we propose our new corpus D-plane which is split into two sub-corpura, D-plane API and D-plane web. Deploying API is based on use texts. In Deploying API, we align 483 documents, all manually. It results in roughly 13,000 and level sentence pairs. For the plane web, this corpus includes different domains. And we also align all of these 750 documents on the one hand manually and on the other hand with automatic alignment methods. In total, we resolved in 30,450 sentence pairs. We analyze our sentence pairs a little bit more. So for example, on the type of simplification. As you can see here, the Bible texts are much stronger simplified than, for example, the new text or the language learn attack. on all level regarding for example lexical simplification, structured simplification, also over all level of simplification. Furthermore, you can see that our deplane corpus has a high variety of different simplification transformations. So for example, in the Deployment API corpus, we have much more reorderings and word additions. Then we have in the Deplane web corpus. On the other hand, in the web corpus we have much more refravings. So let's now see what we can do with this corpus. Hello, I am Omar and now I will talk about the use cases for our dataset deeply. So for the first use case we can evaluate automatic alignment methods. In the recent years there has been a lot of alignment methods but in the context of machine translations where we have have two parallel documents written in different languages and we want to extract alignments of sentences in post-document But in our use case, we are trying to extract alignments between sentences of two. have the same language, having the same content, but they are on a different complexity levels. And now as we have our dataset deep plane which have manually aligned sentences, we can use these sentences as gold standard alignments to evaluate some of the proposed alignment methods. And we did some adaptations to the proposed methods and we have published all these adaptations and the codes to run our experiments in the paper. At the end we concluded that the best alignment of the automatic alignment method to use for German text simplification is the method of mass align. And you can also find the code to run this method on your own documents in the paper. The second use case that we showed in our paper is the case of automatic text simplification. by fine-tuning language models to produce simplified depth text from the complete import text. We have fine-tuned two different models. We have fine-tuned a model of long import to produce document level simplifications and we also fine-tune the normal base long the normal base import to produce sentence level simplifications. You can also find all the checkpoints and you can can look into more details at the scores and evaluation metrics of our experiments in the paper. We concluded that this basic fine tuning could produce or could get scores better than the baseline scores and we propose those results as a benchmark a base benchmark for the problem of automatic text simplification in the future.
